newsitem.title: BOSNIA: ATHLETICS - SPORT RE-BORN IN SARAJEVO.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS - SPORT RE-BORN IN SARAJEVO.

text.p: The heart of the war-ravaged city of Sarajevo began beating again on Monday with the official re-opening of the Kosevo stadium for the International Amateur Athletic Federation's Solidarity meeting.

The meet, attended by 80 athletes, including five Atlanta Olympic champions, was the biggest international event held in the Bosnian capital since the end of the war which followed the break up of Yugoslavia.
Alija Izetbegovic, the president of Bosnia-Herzegovina, launched the meeting being staged where the opening ceremony of the 1984 Winter Olympics was held.

Two dozen white doves, symbolising renewed peace and hope, were released at the end of his speech which followed a welcome by Primo Nebiolo, the president of IAAF and a prime mover in getting the meeting organised.
"Sarajevo, welcome back to world athletics, welcome back to the world of sports," Nebiolo said to rapturous applause from the capacity crowd of 50,000.

Kevan Gosper, a vice-president of the International Olympic Committee deputising for sick IOC president Juan Antonio Samaranch, said: "We are here to help launch a new era for sport in your city and your country."

As he spoke, images of the lighting of the Olympic flame for the 1984 Games were flashed up on a video screen shipped in for the occasion. The same Olympic tower stands starkly today, blackened by shells that rained on the stadium during the war.
A 65-year-old Sarajevo resident named Izo, who did not want to give his family name, said: "It means a lot, not only for me, not only for Sarajevo, but for all of Bosnia-Herzegovina.
"I think we are returning to normal life and this is proof that the world is taking care of us. I am here for the first time since the war broke out and I am happy to see some athletics today."

The stadium represents the symbolic heart of the city, lying as it does between a former maternity hospital and a cemetery where some of the 11,000 Sarajevo residents killed during the war are buried.
All around are signs of the tragic past.

The burned-out skeleton of the Zetra arena where the ice-skating competition was staged in the Games 12 years ago is clearly visible while shell-damaged apartment blocks overlook one side of the stadium.
The IAAF and the IOC contributed $1.5 million towards the rebuilding of the stadium which looked resplendent with new green plastic seating, a newly turfed infield and a Mondo track.
Earlier, Nebiolo made another attack on athletes who had refused to come to the meeting.
